request: gold price calculator - weight in tola, karat 18/21/22/24, today's rate per tola for 24k. gives price

checklist.item: inputs for weight, karat and 24k rate

program:
app "Gold price" coin plum
state tola num = 1
state karat pick K18|K21|K22|K24 = K22
state rate money = 0
state making money = 0
let purity = if(karat = K18, 18, if(karat = K21, 21, if(karat = K22, 22, 24))) / 24
field tola "Weight (tola)"
"Karat" faint
choice karat
field rate "Today's 24k rate per tola"
field making "Making charges per tola"
stat tola * rate * purity + tola * making, "total price"
"Gold value" tola * rate * purity faint
"Making" tola * making faint
"Purity" fixed(purity * 100, 1) "percent" faint
describe:
Gold price, in the plum colours.
Works out:
- purity is 18 when karat is K18, otherwise 21 when karat is K21, otherwise 22 when karat is K22, otherwise 24 divided by 24.
Remembers while you use it: tola, starting at 1; karat, starting at K22; rate, starting at 0; making, starting at 0.
Shows:
- a box to fill in tola, labelled "Weight (tola)".
- text: "Karat".
- a choice of karat.
- a box to fill in rate, labelled "Today's 24k rate per tola".
- a box to fill in making, labelled "Making charges per tola".
- a big number: tola times rate times purity plus tola times making, labelled "total price".
- text: "Gold value", tola times rate times purity.
- text: "Making", tola times making.
- text: "Purity", the fixed of purity times 100, "percent".

program:
app "Rent" home slate
table tenant name text, flat text, rent money, due num 1..28 "Due day", elec money = 0 "Electricity share", paid bool
let expected = sum(tenant, it.rent + it.elec)
let collected = sum(tenant where paid = yes, it.rent + it.elec)
row gap 3
  stat expected, "expected"
  stat collected, "collected"
goal collected, expected, "collected this month"
form tenant, "Add tenant"

  row card tap edit it

      it.name bold
      "Flat" it.flat "due on" it.due faint
    it.rent + it.elec bold
    toggle it.paid
"Not paid yet" head
each tenant where paid = no
  text it.name it.rent + it.elec color bad
button "New month" tap set all tenant.paid = no
describe:
Rent, in the slate colours.
Keeps:
- tenant: name: text; flat: text; rent: money; "Due day": number, 1 to 28; "Electricity share": money, starts at 0; paid: yes or no. Every entry also keeps when it was added.
Works out:
- expected is the sum of its rent plus its elec over the tenant.
- collected is the sum of its rent plus its elec over the tenant where paid is yes.
Shows:
- a big number: expected, labelled "expected".
- a big number: collected, labelled "collected".
- collected out of expected with a progress bar, labelled "collected this month".
- a form to add a tenant.
- for each tenant sorted by its flat:

program:
app "Meeting time" clock ocean
state city pick Islamabad|London|New_York = Islamabad
state t time = 9:00
state bst bool = no
state edt bool = no
let off_src = if(city = Islamabad, 5, if(city = London, if(bst, 1, 0), if(edt, -4, -5)))
let utc = hour(t) - off_src
let shift_ldn = utc + if(bst, 1, 0)
let shift_ny = utc + if(edt, -4, -5)
let shift_isb = utc + 5
let m = if(minute(t) < 10, join("0", minute(t)), join(minute(t)))
"Time is in" faint
choice city
field t "Time"
toggle bst
"London on summer time" faint
toggle edt
"New York on summer time" faint
def zone name text, h num
  row card
    text name bold grow
    text join(h % 24, ":", m) big
    text if(floor(h / 24) > 0, "next day", if(floor(h / 24) < 0, "previous day", "")) faint
zone "Islamabad", shift_isb
zone "London", shift_ldn
zone "New York", shift_ny
describe:
Meeting time, in the ocean colours.
Works out:
- off src is 5 when city is Islamabad, otherwise 1 when bst, otherwise 0 when city is London, otherwise minus 4 when edt, otherwise minus 5.
- utc is the hour of t minus off src.
- shift ldn is utc plus 1 when bst, otherwise 0.
- shift ny is utc plus minus 4 when edt, otherwise minus 5.
- shift isb is utc plus 5.
- m is a value when the minute of t is less than 10, otherwise a value.
Remembers while you use it: city, starting at Islamabad; t, starting at 9:00; bst, starting at no; edt, starting at no.
Shows:
- text: "Time is in".
- a choice of city.
- a box to fill in t, labelled "Time".
- a tick box for bst.
- text: "London on summer time".
- a tick box for edt.
- text: "New York on summer time".
- defines a part called zone, taking name, h.
- the part zone defined in this app, given "Islamabad"; shift isb.
- the part zone defined in this app, given "London"; shift ldn.
- the part zone defined in this app, given "New York"; shift ny.

request: gully match over by over: six dots for this over, tap 0 1 2 3 4 6 or W, keep our score and wickets

each ball circle shows what happened

program:
app "Gully over" ball mint
table ball over num 1.., runs num 0..6, out bool
state ov num = 1 keep
let nb = count(ball where over = ov)
"Over" ov head
row gap 1
  each 1..6 as k
    draw 40, 40 width 40
      circle 20, 20, 17 fill if(nb >= k, if(nth(ball where over = ov sort at, k).out, bad, accent), soft)
      label 20, 21, if(nb >= k, if(nth(ball where over = ov sort at, k).out, "W", join(nth(ball where over = ov sort at, k).runs)), "") bold
if nb < 6
  row gap 1
    each [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6] as v
      button v tap add ball over = ov, runs = v
    button "W" tap add ball over = ov, runs = 0, out = yes
else
  button "New over" tap set ov = ov + 1
row gap 2
  stat sum(ball.runs), "runs"
  stat count(ball where out = yes), "wickets"
"Overs completed:" ov - 1 + if(nb = 6, 1, 0) faint
describe:
Gully over, in the mint colours.
Keeps:
- ball: over: number, at least 1; runs: number, 0 to 6; out: yes or no. Every entry also keeps when it was added.
Works out:
- nb is how many ball entries where over is ov.
Remembers while you use it: ov, starting at 1.
Shows:
- text: "Over", ov.
- for each number from 1 to 6:
  - a drawing made of circles, labels.
- if nb is less than 6:
  - for 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6:
    - a button the value; a tap adds a ball with over set to ov, runs set to the value.

request: Loan EMI: amount, yearly interest rate, months. Show monthly payment and total interest paid. I'd like it to fetch today's bank rates too.

checklist.item: inputs for amount, annual rate and months

program:
app "Loan EMI" money slate
state amount money = 500000
state rate num = 15
state months num = 36
let r = rate / 1200
let emi = if(r = 0, amount / months, amount * r * pow(1 + r, months) / (pow(1 + r, months) - 1))
stack card gap 2
  field amount "Loan amount"
  field rate "Yearly interest rate (percent)"
  field months "Months"
stat round(emi), "monthly payment"
row gap 3
  stat round(emi * months - amount), "total interest"
  stat round(emi * months), "total repayment"
describe:
Loan EMI, in the slate colours.
Works out:
- r is rate divided by 1200.
- emi is amount divided by months when r is 0, otherwise amount times r times the pow of 1 plus r divided by the result of the pow of 1 plus r minus 1.
Remembers while you use it: amount, starting at 500000; rate, starting at 15; months, starting at 36.
Shows:
- a box to fill in amount, labelled "Loan amount".
- a box to fill in rate, labelled "Yearly interest rate (percent)".
- a box to fill in months, labelled "Months".
- a big number: emi rounded, labelled "monthly payment".
- a big number: emi times months minus amount rounded, labelled "total interest".
- a big number: emi times months rounded, labelled "total repayment".

request: monthly budget as a fuel gauge, add spends and the needle goes down. budget 50000

program:
app "Fuel gauge" bolt ocean
setting budget money = 50000 "Monthly budget"
table spend amount money, note text
let used = sum(spend.amount month)
let left = budget - used
let frac = clamp(left / budget, 0, 1)
draw 100, 60 width 240 middle
  arc 50, 55, 40, 270, 450 stroke soft thick 8
  arc 50, 55, 40, 270, 270 + 180 * frac stroke accent thick 8
  line 50, 55, 50 + 34 * sin(-90 + 180 * frac), 55 - 34 * cos(-90 + 180 * frac) stroke ink thick 2
  label 50, 50, left big
"Remaining of" budget faint align center
form spend, "Add spend"
list spend by day
describe:
Fuel gauge, in the ocean colours.

- spend: amount: money; note: text. Every entry also keeps when it was added.
You can change: "Monthly budget": money, starts at 50000.
Works out:
- used is the total amount of spend this month.
- left is budget minus used.
- frac is left divided by budget kept between 0 and 1.
Shows:
- a drawing made of arcs, lines, labels.
- text: "Remaining of", budget.
- a form to add a spend.
- a list of spend by day; tap one to edit it, swipe to remove it.

request: put a chart of the solar units added up for each week, about two months back

checklist.item: a chart of weekly kWh is shown
existing daily entry form still present

program:
app "Solar log" sun ocean
table output day date = today, kwh num 0.. unit "kWh", weather pick Sunny|Cloudy|Rainy
let mon = today - monthday(today) + 1
let wk = today - weekday(today) + 1
stat max(output.kwh), "best day so far (kWh)"
"This month" sum(output.kwh where day >= mon) "kWh" faint
form output, "Add today's output"
"Last 14 days" head
daybars last 14 days, sum(output.kwh where day = it)
"kWh per week, last 8 weeks" head
bars 1..8, sum(output.kwh where day >= wk - 7 * (8 - it) and day < wk - 7 * (7 - it)), join("W", it)
list output
describe:
Solar log, in the ocean colours.
Keeps:
- output: day: date, starts at today; kwh: number, at least 0, in kWh; weather: one of Sunny, Cloudy, Rainy. Every entry also keeps when it was added.
Works out:
- mon is today minus the day of the month of today plus 1.
- wk is today minus the weekday number of today plus 1.
Shows:
- a big number: the highest kwh of output, labelled "best day so far kWh".
- text: "This month", the total kwh of output where day is at least mon, "kWh".
- a form to add a output.
- text: "Last 14 days".
- a bar chart of the total kwh of output where day is the item for each day in the last 14 days.
- text: "kWh per week, last 8 weeks".
- a bar chart of the total kwh of output where day is at least wk minus 7 times the result of 8 minus the item and day is less than wk minus 7 times the result of 7 minus the item for each of number from 1 to 8.
- a list of output; tap one to edit it, swipe to remove it.
